name: Business budget
seoDesc: Business budget: work out income from the income 1 and the income 3. A free finance calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the income 1, the income 3, the income 4 and the donations and the Business budget calculator solves for income. It is built for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Business budget calculator work?
sections.html:
The Business budget calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports income in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the income 1, the income 3, the income 4 and the donations.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Business budget calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Income 2=-income 1 − income 3 − income 4 + total operating income
Interest income=-donations − gifts − grants + total non-operating income − other income
Other one-time costs=-advertising ÷ promotion − company stationery − decorating − deposits − furniture − hardware − legal fees − licenses + total one-time costs − operating cash − purchase price − setup and installation − software − starting inventory
Commissions=-benefits − owner ÷ manager salary − salaries + total salaries
Advertising/marketing=-business insurance − debts − entertainment − franchise fees − health insurance − internet − inventory − equipment leases − maintenance ÷ repairs − miscellaneous + total monthly expenses − office supplies − postage ÷ shipping − professional fees − rent − subscriptions ÷ dues − taxes − telephone − transportation − travel − utilities − website
Total operating income=-total non-operating income + total income

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Business budget calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the income 1, the income 3 and the income 4 — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Business budget calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns income, derived from the income 1, the income 3 and the income 4. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Business budget calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the income 1, the income 3, the income 4 and the donations, which is 49 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter income 1 in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Income 1 opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total operating income = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Business budget calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
